audienceContext: A release review spans several local repositories and must not rely on stale working-tree content.
problem: Release evidence is scattered across repositories, and a local uncommitted change can make an otherwise plausible summary untrustworthy.
outcome: A release lead can inspect one source-cited, commit-pinned brief and see the stale repository that must not enter the evidence set.
viewerUnits: three repositories, seven committed documents, one stale worktree
guardrail: RepoContext labels merchant-web stale and excludes its dirty worktree content from the pinned evidence set.
emotionalTarget: calm confidence before a release decision

beforeState.costShown: The release lead has separate repositories and cannot safely assume every local file is committed.

heroMoment.reveal: The actual Context Brief returns a stable evidence-set identifier with source commits, three repositories, seven documents, and one stale repository.
heroMoment.staging: Hold the live brief result at full-screen scale after a short silence.

segments.action: Show the real demo command and its synthetic-fixture scope.
segments.expectedState: A live stdio MCP workflow is about to inspect three isolated Git repositories.
segments.primaryIdea: Release evidence must be trusted before it is summarized.
segments.wiifm: You see the risk before a summary reaches a release decision.
segments.narration: Three repositories. One release review. And one local change you should not trust.
segments.pronunciation: Repo Context is spoken as two words when it appears in narration.
segments.emphasis: One local change you should not trust.
segments.eyeDirectionTreatment: Start on the command and move to the synthetic fixture scope.

segments.action: Show the real catalog rows and the stale merchant-web state.
segments.expectedState: Three repositories and their current commits are listed; merchant-web is stale.
segments.primaryIdea: The release scope and its risk are explicit.
segments.wiifm: You can see which repository needs attention before trusting the brief.
segments.narration: The catalog makes the scope visible. Atlas API, Merchant Web, and Support Ops. Merchant Web is already marked stale.
segments.pronunciation: Atlas A P I. Merchant Web. Support Ops.
segments.eyeDirectionTreatment: Guide from the three catalog rows to the stale flag.

segments.action: Show the live documentation search and commit comparison.
segments.expectedState: The session finds a release-gate source and compares two Atlas API commits.
segments.primaryIdea: The evidence can be traced to source, not merely summarized.
segments.wiifm: You can check the document and the commit behind a release claim.
segments.narration: Now the brief traces the release gate back to a document and compares the changed path between two Atlas API commits.
segments.eyeDirectionTreatment: Lead from the found source to the single changed path.

segments.action: Show the actual Context Brief and its stable evidence-set identifier.
segments.expectedState: The live MCP response reports three repositories, seven committed documents, one stale repository, and source commits.
segments.primaryIdea: One reviewable brief makes the evidence set explicit.
segments.wiifm: You get a concise release picture without giving up the proof behind it.
segments.narration: Here is the Context Brief. Three repositories. Seven committed documents. One stale worktree. And one stable evidence set you can review before asking an agent to act.
segments.pronunciation: Context Brief. Seven. One stale worktree.
segments.eyeDirectionTreatment: Hold on the counts, then the evidence-set identifier and commit sources.

segments.action: Show the real stale-worktree guardrail from the workflow output.
segments.expectedState: merchant-web is explicitly excluded from pinned evidence because it has an uncommitted change.
segments.primaryIdea: The system explains what it will not trust.
segments.wiifm: You avoid turning dirty local work into release evidence.
segments.narration: The guardrail is just as important. Merchant Web has an uncommitted change, so Repo Context marks it stale and excludes that worktree from pinned evidence.
segments.eyeDirectionTreatment: Focus on stale, then excluded from pinned evidence.

segments.action: Close on the verified workflow outcome and disclosure.
segments.expectedState: The source-cited brief is ready for a release lead; the fixture and synthetic voice are disclosed.
segments.primaryIdea: A release decision can start from evidence rather than assumptions.
segments.wiifm: You can move forward with calm confidence and a reviewable evidence trail.
segments.narration: Repo Context gives your release review a source-cited starting point. Evidence first. Assumptions last.
segments.eyeDirectionTreatment: End on the outcome line and clear synthetic-fixture disclosure.
